text:
alexa: short sync — proposal to move autoscaler decisions for dedicated GPU pools out of the operator and into a tiny adjudicator service.
	a0: motive?
	alexa: operator has accreted lots of responsibility (admit/lease bookkeeping, GC, billing hooks). an adjudicator can centralize policy, make decisions (grant/reserve/defer) and emit short-lived tokens.
	jules: how does this change the warmup/prewarm flow?
	alexa: flow sketch: operator sends intent to adjudicator -> adjudicator returns a signed advice token (or defer) -> operator writes the token to the claims API -> runtime pulls/consumes tokens to prewarm. operator still owns final reservation.
	tao: extra hop. what's the latency impact in the control plane?
	alexa: operator only calls adjudicator when creating a reservation (not on every admit). cached decisions at operator side keep hotpath local. expected p50 < 2ms added for reservation creation.
	jules: autoscaler integration? can adjudicator feed headroom hints?
	alexa: yes. adjudicator emits optional headroom_hint per pool/tenant and can publish events to the autoscaler pubsub. autoscaler can choose to follow hints or operate independently.
	tao: failure modes? adjudicator slow or down?
	alexa: operator has a fallback heuristic and a circuit-breaker. when adjudicator is unavailable we degrade to safe-mode (smaller prewarm budgets, conservative grants).
	jules: double-allocation across regions worry.
	alexa: tokens are region-scoped and include a signed region tag; adjudicator tracks global allocation per-tenant to avoid oversubscribe. token consumption checks signature + region.
	tao: what about billing and chargeback accuracy?
	alexa: adjudicator emits canonical decision events to the ledger. operator records delta events on write; runtime records local consumption events. Reconciliation job computes billing delta (eventual consistency).
	jules: observability?
	alexa: metrics plan: adjudicator: `adjudicator_decisions_granted_total`, `adjudicator_decisions_deferred_total`, `adjudicator_token_latency_ms` histogram, `adjudicator_headroom_hint_gauge`. operator: `operator_tokens_emitted_total`. runtime: `runtime_token_consumed_total`, `runtime_local_prewarm_hits`. add a reconciliation metric `prewarm_billing_delta` from the ledger job.
	tao: security — token forging?
	alexa: tokens signed by adjudicator with key-id header; operator and runtime validate signature and key version. key rotation via k8s secret with versioning.
	jules: GC and orphan tokens?
	alexa: tokens have TTL. adjudicator exposes `/tokens/expire` animation for GC; operator runs periodic reclaim of expired tokens and credits return-to-pool.
	tao: rollout plan?
	alexa: 1) implement adjudicator v1 with readonly policy and tokens (feature-flagged). 2) enable for a small tenant set (10 tenants) and observe prewarm hit-rate + cold-starts. 3) run canary for 48h, then 30% fleets, then default.
	jules: tests?
	alexa: unit tests + integration harness: simulate 200 tenants with churn, chaos tests where adjudicator injects 100-500ms tail latencies, operator restarts, token double-consumption attempts.
	tao: backwards compatibility with current token/claim system?
	alexa: operator will support both v1 token and adjudicator tokens. runtime consumes tokens by priority: adjudicator tokens > legacy tokens, allowing staged migration.
	jules: perf knobs — how often should runtime poll claims?
	alexa: default 5s poll with jitter; operator caches adjudicator responses for 30s. tune after canary.
	devops-bot: ci/adjudicator build: green; ci/operator: pending.
	alexa: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, API surface and perf microbenchmarks. tagging @tao @jules
